# A bill with a tax entry, applying both splits of the transaction that paid
# it.
#
# The cost and the GST were separated when the supplier was paid, so the
# transaction holds a split for each — and the bill books both accounts. The
# block names both, so nothing is left for the run to work out: both move to
# the payable and come to 113.00, which is what the bill owes.
#
# What this fixture produces: the payable settled, `Expenses:Supplies:USD` at
# 100.00, `Liabilities:Tax:GST USD` at 13.00 and the card at −113.00.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
taxtable "GST"
  entry:
    account: "Liabilities:Tax:GST USD"
    rate: 13.0%
    type: PERCENT

bill "BILL-GST-003"
  vendor_id: "V-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-02-18
  entry:
    date: 2026-02-18
    description: "Supplies"
    account: "Expenses:Supplies:USD"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: true
    tax_included: false
    tax_table: "GST"
  posted:
    date: 2026-02-18
    due: 2026-03-18
    ap_account: "Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD"
    memo: "Bill BILL-GST-003"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-18
    amount: 113
    account: "Liabilities:Credit Card USD"
    Transaction "ccddeeff00112233445566778899aabb"
      PaymentSplit "ddeeff00112233445566778899aabbcc"
      PaymentSplit "eeff00112233445566778899aabbccdd"
